blocks.text: Jali Din grows reckless on this page, plundering the country and assuming that fear alone will keep the Sikhs shut inside their fortresses. Against that pressure, Baj Singh would not flee or accept the shame of simply watching the region be ravaged.

Instead he launches a night march from Lohgarh and falls on the enemy before they are prepared. The attack is remembered as swift and predatory, like a hawk on its prey, because it overturns Jali Din’s confidence in a single stroke.
The episode closes with a clean reversal of fortune. The sudden attack on Jali Din ends with his death and restores Sikh initiative after a moment of imperial boasting.
